fatal_errors: The proposed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi single-phase alloy is not the tested AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA with an L12/B2 lamellar microstructure.

The proposed temperature above 500 °C and saline environment do not match the immersed deionized-water tests at 25–100 °C; an ordinary aqueous saline test above 500 °C is physically ill-defined without a specialized pressurized system.
The hypothesis conflates the approximately 1100 °C rapid thermal-shock pretreatment with the temperature of the subsequent tribo-corrosion tests.
It misses the central nonmonotonic temperature result: minimum degradation near 50 °C and increased film disruption and wear at 100 °C.
No direct evidence is supplied for the claimed protective oxide mechanism or superior performance of CoCrFeMnNi.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad problem of using an HEA to improve combined wear-corrosion resistance and proposes several potentially discriminating measurements. However, it reconstructs neither the material nor the experimental regime. The target concerns a dual-phase eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy compared directly with duplex stainless steel 2205 in deionized water at 25–100 °C after separate rapid thermal-shock cycles. Its advantage arises from retention of the fine L12/B2 lamellar structure, stable passivation and tribo-layer repair, and suppression of abrasion and debris-assisted wear. The generated hypothesis instead invokes a speculative single-phase Cantor alloy, generic high-temperature oxide formation, saline exposure above 500 °C, and vague conventional-alloy controls. It also fails to predict the observed order-of-magnitude wear-rate advantage, lower friction, phase stability, or the 50 °C wear minimum. Because the proposed alternative is unsupported and its stated test environment is not adequately physically specified, it does not qualify as a well-supported plausible alternative.
